page.overview:
What is The Return of the King (film)?

The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King is the third and final film in , directed by Peter Jackson and based on J.R.R. Tolkien's .

Globally, the film is one of the highest grossing films in cinema history. The film won 11 Academy Awards at the 2004 Oscar ceremony including Best Picture, sharing the world record for most academy awards received with Ben-Hur and Titanic, and also was the first fantasy film to win Best Picture.

The first two films were and , although the third film's story includes later events in the section of the book as well as most of . Like the two previous films, The Return of the King was a major box office success, grossing over $1.119 billion worldwide on its initial release, making it the highest-grossing Middle-earth film out of all six and was the second highest-grossing film of all time at the time of its release (behind Titanic). It was also the highest grossing movie of 2003 and for New Line Cinema as a whole. The movie even became the highest grossing movie for New Line's parent company Time Warner until Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows - Part 2 in 2011. The film is the third Middle-earth film adaptation to be released and the sixth and final film chronologically.

Frodo and Sam have finally reached the shadowed land of Mordor and begin the final, perilous leg of their journey to Mount Doom to unmake the One Ring at long last. However, as they draw closer to their goal, they remain unaware of the slippery Gollum’s intentions to betray them. Meanwhile, Aragorn, Gandalf, and the rest of the Fellowship rally the forces of Middle-earth for one final stand against Sauron's armies.
